claims.statement: The app defines three build types: debug (no minification, `.debug` applicationId suffix so it installs alongside release, full ABI for emulators), release (R8 minification + resource shrinking), and benchmark (created via `initWith(getByName("release"))`, debug-signed, `isDebuggable = false`, adding `x86_64` ABI on top of release's arm64-v8a, `matchingFallbacks` to release).

Release builds ship arm64-v8a only (minSdk 33 devices are all 64-bit) and restrict resources to `resConfigs("zh", "en")`, enabling R8 minification plus resource shrinking with `proguard-android-optimize.txt`; the audit records the resulting release APK at ~6.2 MB. debug/benchmark keep multiple ABIs for emulator compatibility.

Release signing reads the gitignored `keystore.properties` (storeFile/storePassword/keyAlias/keyPassword); when it is missing, local builds fall back to debug signing with a warning, but passing `-PrequireReleaseSigning=true` (release/CI scenario) makes the build fail outright to prevent shipping a debug-signed "release" artifact.

The `check` lifecycle task aggregates root-level `spotlessCheck` and `verifyProductArchitecture` plus every subproject's `check`; each subproject's `check` also depends on its own `spotlessCheck`, so a full `check` runs formatting, architecture assertions, and all module unit tests across debug/release/benchmark variants.

`verifyProductArchitecture` is orchestration in the root `build.gradle.kts` `doLast` block whose rule body was extracted (m-10, 2026-10-15 review) into the `buildSrc` object `cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.verify.ProductArchitectureVerification`: `verify(rootDir)` walks kt/kts/java/xml/toml files (skipping build/.gradle/.git/.idea AND buildSrc to avoid self-trigger from rule-text counterexamples), collects ALL violations into a LinkedHashSet, and the task throws one `GradleException` with the joined list (collection-style, not fail-fast). The rule behavior is unit-tested by `ProductArchitectureVerificationTest`; there is still no incremental or allowlist mode, so any new file/module enters the next scan.

The gate enforces the product module inventory and per-module hygiene: all 15 modules (including `:core:skin` and `:benchmark`) must appear in `settings.gradle.kts`, and every module directory must keep a local `.gitignore` containing `/build/`, `/.cxx/`, `/.externalNativeBuild/`, and `/captures/`.

Hilt assembly points are hard-gated: `MelodyApplication` (`@HiltAndroidApp`), `MainActivity` (`@AndroidEntryPoint`), `AppMediaSessionService` in :player (`@AndroidEntryPoint`), and `PlayerViewModel` (`@HiltViewModel`) must exist with their annotations, and the six required SingletonComponent Hilt modules (app/di: CoroutineModule, LoggerModule, PlayerModule; data/di: RepositoryModule, DatabaseModule, DataStoreModule) must exist as `@Module @InstallIn(SingletonComponent::class)` objects.

The gate pins the architecture docs: `docs/architecture/PLAYBACK_STATE_MACHINE.md` must exist and document the playback state/sync terms (idle..error states plus AppMediaSessionService, PlaybackController, ControllerPlaybackStateSynchronizer, PlayerControllerStateFacade, PlayerMediaEventFacade), and `docs/refactor/PRODUCT_REFACTOR_AUDIT.md` must track Verified / Still Not Fully Proven sections plus the release, benchmark, and test validation commands.

The gate locks the :benchmark module shape: the build file must use the Android test plugin, `targetProjectPath = ":app"`, and depend on `androidx.benchmark.macro.junit4`; `StartupBenchmark` must keep MacrobenchmarkRule, StartupTimingMetric, StartupMode.COLD, startActivityAndWait, and `packageName = "cn.com.dcsgo.mihx"`.

Performance observability is gate-anchored: `PerformanceTrace` must exist in :core:common, `MusicRepository` must keep the `music_import_scan`/`music_import_folder` trace operations, `PlaybackController` must keep `controller_play_queue`/`controller_prepare_queue`/`controller_sync_queue`/`play_next_command`, and `PlaybackWindowPerformanceShapeTest` must keep covering the 100/500/1000-song queue sizes with the 71-item window bound.

Historical regressions are banned at source-scan level: no references to the legacy `com.dcsgo.data.model` package, no `PlayerViewModelComponents`/`PlayerViewModelComponentFactory` (the old manual assembly hub, deliberately replaced by PlayerRuntime and injected facade/graph objects), and no Android Things dependency strings.

Module dependency boundaries are gate-enforced: feature build files must not declare `project(":data")`, `project(":player")`, or any `project(":feature:…")`; feature/domain/player sources must not import `cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.data.(repository|local).*`; MusicRepository must not declare the four domain repository interfaces as supertypes while the four `*RepositoryAdapter.kt` files must exist and implement them; and the whole `:player` module (kt/java/xml) must not reference the stale `cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.data.player` package since its classes moved to `cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.player` (matching the module namespace) — this rule prevents regression to the old implementation package.

UI routing patterns are gate-enforced: features must expose Route+Screen composables (lyrics, settings, play stats, quick-skip, version management are individually checked), the overlay routing files (AppOverlay.kt/AppOverlayHost.kt/OverlayRoute.kt) must not reappear, :feature:home must not import `cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.ui.lyrics` directly, and :core:model must contain no res XML and no UI resource id references.

Privacy-sensitive capability startup is gate-enforced: Bluetooth monitoring must never initialize at app startup (PlayerStartupFacade must not contain `Bluetooth`, and the four startup-path files must not request notification/Bluetooth permissions); SettingsScreen must expose the user-triggered Bluetooth controls; and Bluetooth playback monitoring and playback notification must be persisted PlayerSettingsRepository/DataStore keys surfaced through PlayerUiState rather than app-shell local remember state, with PermissionCoordinator supporting onGranted callbacks.

Two product-wide code quality rules are machine-enforced: LazyColumn `items`/`itemsIndexed` calls in app/core/feature must declare a stable `key` within 160 characters (bare `item { }` is banned), and direct `android.util.Log` calls are banned everywhere except `AppLogger.kt` itself — all logging goes through AppLog/AppLogger.

Manifest placement rules are gate-enforced: `AppMediaSessionService` must be declared by the :player manifest (never the :app manifest), and the :app manifest must not declare READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE; READ_MEDIA_AUDIO is the one allowed exception so an already-granted device can fast-scan via java.io.File, with SAF document-tree access remaining the primary path and fallback.

The gate parses the app release build type by brace-pairing, not the old first-closing-brace regex: `extractBracedBlock(appBuildText, "release")` counts `{`/`}` and returns the balanced block (fixing the review-named truncation when nested lambdas appear), then requires `isMinifyEnabled = true` and `isShrinkResources = true`. Because the extraction tools still favor flat blocks, the signing decision is deliberately kept outside `buildTypes` via a `releaseSigningConfig` val and the release block holds only flat assignments (`signingConfig = releaseSigningConfig`, `isMinifyEnabled`, `isShrinkResources`, `proguardFiles(...)`, `ndk { abiFilters += "arm64-v8a" }`).

Privacy/backup exclusion is a gate-enforced release checklist: both `backup_rules.xml` (full-backup-content) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (cloud-backup + device-transfer) must exclude the legacy SharedPreferences files, the full melody.db family (db/journal/shm/wal), the player_settings and playback_state DataStore files, and the album-art caches; adding a new persisted file requires updating both rule files or the architecture check fails.

Room schema JSONs are immutable snapshots whose version history is tamper-evident: schema v1 must not contain `quick_skip_short_play_counts`, v2 must contain it but not `lrcUri`, v3 must contain `lrcUri`. Since m-4 the migration objects live in `data/.../local/migration/MelodyMigrations.kt` (public, so the migration regression test references the same instances as production): it must register `Migration(1, 2)` and `Migration(2, 3)`, and `DatabaseModule` must call `addMigrations(*MelodyMigrations.ALL)`.

The Room schema workflow: :data exports schemas via `ksp { arg("room.schemaLocation", "$projectDir/schemas") }`, MelodyDatabase declares `version = 11, exportSchema = true` (v11, 2026-10-20, added the `word_preferences` voting table via `MIGRATION_10_11` / `WordPreferenceEntity`); entity/DAO changes require bumping the version, building :data to auto-generate the new JSON in data/schemas/, adding a `Migration(N, N+1)` in `data/.../local/migration/MelodyMigrations.kt` and appending it to the trailing `ALL: Array<Migration>` array (declared last so object properties initialize in order; DatabaseModule registers via `addMigrations(*MelodyMigrations.ALL)`), adding a focused unit test for complex migrations, and never hand-editing existing schema JSONs.

The :benchmark module provides three Macrobenchmark entry points: StartupBenchmark (two cold-start tests — StartupTimingMetric, 5 iterations each — comparing CompilationMode.None() vs CompilationMode.Partial(Require) via pressHome()+startActivityAndWait), ScrollBenchmark (FrameTimingMetric, 5 iterations, 3 down + 3 up home-screen swipes), and BaselineProfileGenerator (BaselineProfileRule.collect that writes app/src/main/baselineProfiles/baseline-prof.txt); it suppresses the EMULATOR error via testInstrumentationRunnerArguments and enables only the benchmark build type via androidComponents.beforeVariants.

Baseline Profile operations: the bundled baseline-prof.txt (~2425 rules, generated on a Pixel 6 emulator) is packaged into release builds and installed by androidx.profileinstaller to speed cold start and first-screen scroll; regeneration runs via `:app:generateBaselineProfile` or `:benchmark:connectedCheck` and requires a real device/emulator, with MIUI ROMs potentially blocking macrobenchmark's automated permission/frame-confirmation steps and physical-device cold-start acceptance still pending (emulator median ~810 ms, software-rendered).

PerformanceTrace is an explicit observability policy, not a logging side effect: `isEnabled` initializes from BuildConfig.DEBUG so debug builds trace everything while release is intentionally silent, an `allow`/`disallow` allowlist lets critical operations emit traces in release, `measure`/`log` emit through AppLog.info with redacted metadata, and core/common explicitly enables buildConfig for BuildConfig.DEBUG.

AppLog/AppLogger is the only logging channel: AndroidAppLogger gates debug/info/warning behind BuildConfig.DEBUG while error always emits, and every message and stack trace passes through `redactSensitiveValuesForLog()` which replaces content:// URIs, file:// URIs, Bluetooth MACs, device names, and Windows/POSIX paths with redacted placeholders — so release builds expose only sanitized error logs; AppLog.install(AndroidAppLogger(BuildConfig.DEBUG)) wires it in MelodyApplication.onCreate and the uncaught-exception hook also logs through AppLog.

Version compatibility constraints: Kotlin 2.0.21 requires the built-in compose compiler plugin (`org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose`) and forbids the old `composeOptions { kotlinCompilerExtensionVersion }` block; KSP 2.0.21-1.0.28 must prefix-match the Kotlin version exactly; Media3 1.9.0 pairs with the Jellyfin FFmpeg extension 1.9.0+1; Room 2.6.1, Hilt 2.52, AGP 8.13.2, minSdk 33 / targetSdk 36 with Java 11 bytecode; LiteRT 1.4.1 / WorkManager 2.9.1; effective versionName is 3.11.0 / versionCode 46 — `app/build.gradle.kts` and `gradle/libs.versions.toml` are authoritative, and CLAUDE.md's Key Versions table now matches this config (its "Room 当前 v10" line lags the actual v11).

R8 keep rules in app/proguard-rules.pro preserve manifest entry points (MelodyApplication, MainActivity, AppMediaSessionService), Hilt/Room/Media3 reflection attributes, MelodyDatabase and entity classes for diagnosability, and the Jellyfin FFmpeg decoder classes (`FfmpegAudioDecoder`, `FfmpegLibrary`) because `:player`'s `FfmpegPcmDecoder` (now at `cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.player`) drives the package-private Media3 FFmpeg decoder reflectively via a `Class.forName`-based `FfmpegLibraryProbe` — renaming or stripping these breaks the FFmpeg decode path. (The keep rule still lists the AppMediaSessionService name under the legacy `cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.data.player` FQN.)

Deterministic Windows verification depends on `kotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process`: the Kotlin daemon used to fail creating client marker files on Windows and fall back mid-build, so compilation runs inside the Gradle daemon — which means `org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx2048m` is the effective compile heap (kotlin.daemon.jvmargs only applies out-of-process; CLAUDE.md's 3072 MB note is stale), alongside `org.gradle.parallel=true` and `org.gradle.caching=true`.

`android.nonTransitiveRClass=true` scopes each module's R class to its own declared resources, so resources must not be referenced across module boundaries via R classes — complementary to the gate rule that :core:model may carry no UI resource ids (mapping belongs in :core:ui or the owning feature, e.g. PlayMode.iconRes()).

Spotless is the formatting gate and must stay catalog-managed: the root build applies `alias(libs.plugins.spotless)` and defines kotlin/kotlinGradle/androidXml format rules (trim trailing whitespace, end with newline), the catalog must keep the spotless plugin entry, and both the root and each subproject's `check` must depend on `spotlessCheck` (both facts gate-enforced).

Device-dependent validation commands: `:app:connectedAndroidTest` (Compose instrumentation) and `:benchmark:connectedCheck` (macrobenchmarks including Baseline Profile generation) require a real device or emulator, whereas full `test` runs on the JVM across debug/release/benchmark unit-test variants; media-key/service behavior and the ActivityResult permission path are still verified primarily through JVM planner/facade/policy tests rather than end-to-end device tests.

OpenWiki pages are generated artifacts refreshed by on-demand `openwiki code --update` runs; hand-editing them is discouraged — source code and docs/ are authoritative (per AGENTS.md), and some architecture facts in docs/ are gate-locked by verifyProductArchitecture. Two GitHub Actions workflows exist: `pr-check.yml` (pull requests + pushes to main, skipped for docs/**/openwiki/**.md) and `release.yml` (v* tags / workflow_dispatch) — both first run `./gradlew check :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest :buildSrc:test` (assembleDebugAndroidTest compiles instrumentation sources without a device; :buildSrc:test covers the gate rule body), then release builds the signed APK, apksigner-verifies it, and publishes a GitHub Release.

The `:app` manifest's `<application>` sets `android:largeHeap="true"` (declared in v3.11.0), and release ships only `arm64-v8a` via `ndk.abiFilters` with `resConfigs("zh", "en")` trimming dependency-library translation resources; because minSdk is 33 all real devices are 64-bit.

The `pr-check.yml` and `release.yml` `check` jobs run `./gradlew check :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest :buildSrc:test` on ubuntu-24.04 with JDK 17; `:app:assembleDebugAndroidTest` only compiles the instrumentation test sources (no device, catching UI signature drift) and `:buildSrc:test` unit-tests the verifyProductArchitecture rule body.

Room v11 (versionCode 46 / versionName 3.11.0) migration adds the `word_preferences` emotion-word listening-preference voting table (`word` TEXT PRIMARY KEY, `likeVotes`/`dislikeVotes`/`updatedAt` INTEGER) via `MIGRATION_10_11`, backed by `WordPreferenceEntity` with `@Entity(tableName = "word_preferences")`.
